issues.failure_explanation: An RKBS is continuously included in the pointwise function space, but its image need not be closed in the supremum norm. In fact, under an infinite-dimensional compact embedding, the image cannot be a closed infinite-dimensional subspace with an equivalent inverse. Moreover, continuous inclusion of bounded functions into an L1 space does not preserve closedness. Thus \hat E=(E,\|\cdot\|_F) need not be complete or a closed L1 subspace, so Theorem \ref{theorem:Lpembed} cannot be applied. The proof also upgrades that theorem's isomorphic embedding to an isometry without justification.

failure_location.quote: Recall that $E$ is an RKBS, so it is a closed subspace of $F=\ell_\infty(X)$. Therefore $E$ is a closed subspace of $L_1(X)$ because $\ell_\infty(X)$ embeds continuously to $L_1$, so is $\hat{E}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, the proof must construct an appropriate complete closed L1 subspace and establish a valid isomorphic embedding without assuming that the weaker supremum norm makes E complete.
issues.overall_effect: The central passage from entropy/type information to an Lp representation fails, invalidating the main embedding theorem and all application corollaries derived from it.

issues.failure_explanation: For any nonzero x in the E-unit ball, after the signs are realized the supremum may choose x_i=epsilon_i x. Its left side is then at least \|x\|_F for every n. Under the finite polynomial entropy bounds used later, the claimed right side tends to zero with n. Standard Dudley bounds take a supremum over a fixed indexed stochastic process, not independent sign-adaptive choices of every x_i. The proof's chaining and Massart step do not remove this adaptivity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, the stochastic quantity must be reformulated so that its index set is fixed independently of the signs, followed by a new argument connecting that different quantity to the type estimate needed later.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted entropy-to-Rademacher decay is false, so the main proof cannot infer its Rademacher estimate or any subsequent type and embedding conclusion.
issues.title: Dudley bound is false because the supremum adapts every summand to the Rademacher signs
issues.why_classification: The theorem is contradicted directly and repairing it changes the quantity at the heart of the proof, requiring new global reasoning.

issues.failure_explanation: If A is a singleton containing any tuple for which the Rademacher sum is nonzero with positive probability, the right side is zero because log|A|=0 while the left side is positive. The proof also cannot apply Hoeffding's lemma to exp(\|lambda sigma_i a_i\|): the norm removes the sign, so this is a positive deterministic exponential rather than a centered signed variable. diagnostic_evidence.quote: By the fact that $|U_j|\le m^{k}$, $\|2^kx_i\|_F\le 1$ and using Lemma \ref{lemma:Kahane}

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis only controls vectors normalized in the stronger E norm, whereas type requires homogeneous control by their F norms. The proof groups vectors by F norm but then invokes the hypothesis without establishing E-unit normalization; the quoted assertion \|2^k x_i\|_F<=1 is also unrelated to the U_j definition and would not imply \|2^k x_i\|_E<=1. A concrete counterexample is E={x:sum 4^j|x_j|^2<infinity} embedded in F=l1. Its E-unit ball satisfies the p'=2 estimate by coordinatewise Khintchine and summability of 2^{-j}, but E contains all finite sequences and with the l1 norm has no type s>1: the first n unit vectors give Rademacher norm n versus n^{1/s}. Moreover, (E,\|\cdot\|_F) is generally incomplete.
